info.desc: Pyromania is the third studio album by British rock band Def Leppard, released in 1983. It broke the band across North America and in Japan, and would sell over 10 million copies in the US alone. It featured new guitarist Phil Collen and was produced by Robert John "Mutt" Lange. The album was partially recorded with original guitarist Pete Willis, whose rhythm guitar tracks and backing vocals appear on all songs. podcast.body: This album, produced by Mutt Lange, was incredibly expensive to make, costing around $3 million. Chris Berkett was responsible for programming all the drums on a Fairlight CMI, a process that took six weeks of meticulous typing in musical code for every single event. The drums had to be re-recorded from the original floppy disks three times because the analog master tapes wore out from repeated transfers and overdubs. "not wonder that album cost something like $3 million to make."

podcast.body: This album, released in January 1983, served as a significant breakthrough for Def Leppard, reaching number two on the Billboard album chart. It produced four hit singles, including "Rock of Ages," "Photograph," "Foolin'," and "Too Late for Love," solidifying the band's presence in the mainstream. "Deaf Leopard's breakthrough was the album Pyromania which burst onto our radio's and television in January 1983."
